title: L'Odissea di Cleopatra
canon: Present-day high-concept science-fiction drama. Cleopatra "Cleo" Modica, 35, a Sicilian-American social worker born and raised in Brooklyn and now living in Los Angeles, divorced mother of two, transfers her consciousness into a parallel version of her own life every time she falls asleep — waking in Modica in Sicily, in Tokyo, in Poland and beyond, fluent in each life's language, fighting to get home to her kids. The multiverse announces itself only through glitches in ordinary reality: deja vu, lagging reflections, impossible coincidences.
look: Photorealistic contemporary naturalism — no sci-fi hardware anywhere; the multiverse shows only as quiet glitches: a reflection that lags, a doubled self, a faint ripple in the air. Chiaroscuro single-source lighting with deep shadow; a palette of cool deep blues and purples cut by warm amber highlights. Each dimension keeps its own truthful light — LA golden dusk and sodium-and-neon night, hard Sicilian sun through shutter slats, rain-wet Tokyo LED glow. Fine film grain, muted print color, full-bleed widescreen anamorphic frames.
note: Period/place come from the ruled canon: the project file logline and 310-cleopatra-syno (Brooklyn-born, now LA, parallel dimensions in Modica/Tokyo/Poland on the same contemporary timeline). The look is lifted from the syno's approved poster concepts (Fractured Veil / Echoes in the Dark / Awakening Threshold): chiaroscuro, cool blues + amber, film grain, glitch shown subtly. NOTE: 00f-series-overview proposes an all-LA 'reigns' reset that is still flagged ⚑ Needs Marco — this spec follows the ruled canon (LA home + global parallels), which also matches the existing stills (Modica, Tokyo, LA). CAST WARNING: the existing AI stills do NOT share one Cleo face — at least four different women across the set (stoop portrait, apartment window, Tokyo, boardroom). I locked all six shots to 07-cleopatra-01-cleo-k2a.png (the best-quality face: dark curly hair, olive skin, small cross necklace) so the regenerated set finally holds one woman. 07-sleep-threshold.png (futuristic bedroom) is off-canon and 08-rival-edge.png is letterboxed; both are superseded, not referenced. Hollywood.jpg and Shibuya_Crossing.jpg are the only real photographs and carry location truth for the LA and Tokyo shots. 2026-07-16: appended six STORY shots per the Story Law (STORY-LAW.md) — beats mined from the Genesis canon treatment (Eps 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 9): the Modica sedation she loses, Ezra's childhood-drawings reveal in Poland, the kids inheriting the glitch, Brill reaching her daughter, the Tokyo temple controlled crossing, and the LA convergence. Every Cleo shot keeps the locked face ref 07-cleopatra-01-cleo-k2a.png; glitches stay wrong-reflections/ripples only.

stills.notes: The inciting image — Episode 1's first glitch. Ref carries Cleo's face and hair only; composition replaces the watermarked Cleo-glitch composite. Avoids the failure of showing sci-fi effects: the glitch is purely a wrong reflection.
stills.prompt: A cramped 1960s apartment bathroom in East Hollywood, Los Angeles, present day, two in the morning. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace, in a worn grey sweatshirt, stands frozen at the sink — and in the medicine-cabinet mirror her reflection has not kept up: it stands a half-beat behind her, palm pressed flat against the inside of the glass as if from the other side. The only light is the single warm bulb above the mirror, hard on her face, and a thin cold blue spill from a streetlit window down the hallway behind her; the corners of the room fall to black. Chipped white tile, a child's bath toy on the tub rim, a shower curtain half drawn. Full-bleed widescreen frame, modern anamorphic digital cinema still, fine film grain, muted print color. No letterbox, no black bars, no borders. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The signature crossing — Episode 1, waking as her Sicilian self. Ref locks the face so this dimension reads as the SAME woman; the existing modica still had the right room but a drifting face. Light law: every source is the shuttered sun.

stills.prompt: Shibuya scramble crossing, Tokyo, present day, a rainy night. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, wrapped in a charcoal wool coat, stands perfectly still under a clear plastic umbrella at the center of the crossing while blurred crowds of commuters with dark umbrellas stream around her in every direction — she is looking up at the towers as if seeing the city for the first time. Every light in the frame comes from the giant LED billboards and stacked signage around the crossing — cyan, red and yellow washes shifting across wet asphalt and the skin of her umbrella — plus white car headlights streaking through the rain; no other light sources, sky pure black overhead. stills.prompt: A 24-hour diner on a boulevard in Los Angeles, present day, deep in the night, photographed from the wet sidewalk through the plate-glass window. Inside, a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace, in a worn canvas jacket, sits in a red vinyl booth staring at the phone in her hands — and faintly overlaid on the glass, her reflection from the street side shows the same woman standing outside in a tailored coat, looking in at herself. The two faces are identical. Light comes only from the diner's warm fluorescent interior spilling through the window, the red and yellow neon of the diner sign burning above, and cold blue passing headlights reflected in the wet pavement. Rain-specked glass, coffee machines and a lone waitress deep in the background. Full-bleed widescreen frame, modern anamorphic digital cinema still, fine film grain, muted print color. No letterbox, no black bars, no borders. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: The home-dimension anchor: her real, tired LA life with the kids she crosses worlds to get back to. Real Hollywood Blvd photo carries the true streetscape — mixed-use towers, billboards, theater marquees at blue hour.
stills.prompt: Hollywood Boulevard near Vine Street, Los Angeles, present day, blue hour just after sunset. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, in a denim jacket over work clothes with a heavy shoulder bag, walks toward camera holding the hands of her two children, a boy and a girl, small figures against the lit-up boulevard — glass apartment blocks, billboard scaffolds, old theater facades receding behind them. The sky is deep cobalt; all other light is the city's own: white and amber storefront spill, glowing billboard faces, sodium streetlamps just waking, and red tail-light streaks from passing cars on the wet-sheened asphalt. She looks exhausted and utterly determined to hold on. Full-bleed widescreen frame, modern anamorphic digital cinema still, fine film grain, muted print color. stills.prompt: An extreme cinematic close-up portrait of a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and expressive brown eyes, present day, her face filling most of the frame with a resolute, haunted expression. stills.notes: STORY (Ep 1): her first crossing is punished — the Modica dimension sedates her by force and she loses. A stranger reads it instantly: a woman fighting an injection while her own family holds her down. Different beat from waking-in-modica (that is the waking; this is the consequence).
stills.prompt: A doctor's ground-floor study in an old baroque townhouse in Modica, Sicily, present day, late afternoon. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace, in a white cotton nightgown, is being held down in a cracked leather armchair by two anguished middle-aged relatives while a heavyset doctor in rolled shirtsleeves drives a syringe toward her bared forearm — she is mid-fight, wrenching her arm away, mouth open in protest, her free hand knocking a metal tray of instruments off the side table, glass vials caught falling in the air. All light in the frame is low hard Sicilian sun cutting through half-closed wooden shutters, throwing bright raking bars across the struggle and the terrazzo floor; everything the bars miss falls into deep warm shadow. Shelves of old medical books, a crucifix above the desk. Full-bleed widescreen frame, modern anamorphic digital cinema still, fine film grain, muted print color. No letterbox, no black bars, no borders. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: STORY (Ep 2): Ezra, the Polish-dimension ex-convict mentor, lays out her own childhood crayon drawings — each one a dimension she now travels. The frame shows the reveal happening and what it means: she was marked from the start, and someone kept the proof. Drawings depict places, not words, so the no-text law holds.
stills.prompt: A cluttered one-room flat in the Praga district of Warsaw, Poland, present day, winter dusk. A gaunt white-haired man in a threadbare cardigan, hands scarred and tattooed like an old convict's, spreads a dozen yellowed children's crayon drawings across a scarred wooden table in front of a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, wrapped in a borrowed grey wool coat — each drawing unmistakably shows a different city in a child's hand: a white Sicilian hill town, a rainy crossing of glowing towers, a snowy street exactly like the one outside the window — and she has one hand pressed to her mouth, the other touching a drawing, recognizing her own childhood work. The only light is a single low tungsten desk lamp pulled over the drawings, hard and warm on the paper and both faces, against a cold blue winter window losing its light behind them; the rest of the room falls to black. Full-bleed widescreen frame, modern anamorphic digital cinema still, fine film grain, muted print color. No letterbox, no black bars, no borders. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: STORY (Ep 4): the cost of the kids-anchor — her children are inheriting the ability. The glitch stays inside the law (a wrong reflection only): the boy's reflection has turned to look while the boy still writes. The dropping plate makes the stakes legible to a stranger.
stills.prompt: The small kitchen of a 1960s apartment in East Hollywood, Los Angeles, present day, night. A nine-year-old boy does homework at the kitchen table while his younger sister colors beside him — but in the black window glass behind them the boy's reflection has stopped writing and turned fully around to stare into the room, though the boy himself is still bent over his page. In the near foreground his mother, a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair and a small cross necklace, in a worn grey sweatshirt, has frozen mid-step seeing it, a dinner plate slipping from her hands, caught in the air just before it shatters. The only light is the single warm hanging bulb over the table, hard on the children and the falling plate, and a thin cold blue streetlight spill through the window carrying the wrong reflection; the corners of the kitchen fall to black. stills.prompt: A chain-link fenced elementary schoolyard in East Hollywood, Los Angeles, present day, late golden afternoon. On the far side of the fence a composed grey-haired man in an immaculate charcoal suit crouches to a child's eye level, speaking through the chain-link to a small dark-haired seven-year-old girl and holding something out to her in his open palm — while in the foreground her mother, a 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, in a denim jacket over work clothes, sprints toward them across the sidewalk, mid-shout, her heavy shoulder bag dropped on the pavement behind her. All light is hard low Los Angeles sun raking across the asphalt, throwing long shadows from the fence diamonds over the man and the girl and flaring on the running woman's face; palm trees and a faded bungalow school building behind. stills.notes: STORY (Ep 7): she fights back — the first deliberate, controlled crossing, trained by the Tokyo Zen-master version of Ezra. The stake is visible: effort in her fists, ripple in the air, and her shadow on the shoji a half-beat out of alignment (glitch law: ripple + wrong shadow only, no hardware).
stills.prompt: The wooden meditation hall of a small Zen temple in the Yanaka district of Tokyo, present day, before dawn. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, in simple dark practice clothes, sits half-lotus on a tatami platform, eyes shut with fierce effort, fists clenched on her knees — the air around her shoulders carries a faint concentric ripple like disturbed water, and her shadow cast on the paper shoji screen behind her sits a half-beat out of alignment with her body, its head turned when hers is not. An elderly shaven-headed Japanese monk kneels facing her, leaning in intently, one hand lifted as if deciding whether to steady her or stop her. All light is a row of candle flames along the altar, warm and hard on both faces, against the first grey-blue of dawn glowing through the shoji paper; the timber ceiling falls to black. Full-bleed widescreen frame, modern anamorphic digital cinema still, fine film grain, muted print color. No letterbox, no black bars, no borders. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: STORY (Ep 9): the destination of the odyssey — the dimensions bleed into her home city, shown entirely within the glitch law: every storefront window reflects a different world while the street stays real. She is running her kids OUT of it, so a stranger reads flight and collapse, not a mood piece. Hollywood.jpg carries the true boulevard geometry.
stills.prompt: Hollywood Boulevard near Vine Street, Los Angeles, present day, night, the sidewalk almost empty. A 35-year-old Italian-American woman with dark curly hair, in a denim jacket, runs down the sidewalk toward camera pulling her two children by the hands — a boy and a small girl, both looking back — while every plate-glass storefront window they pass reflects a different world instead of the boulevard: one pane holds hard white Sicilian daylight on stone, the next a rain-streaked wall of Tokyo neon, the next a grey snowy Warsaw street — the reflections wrong, the street itself real. The boulevard's own light rules the frame: sodium streetlamps, old theater marquee spill and glowing billboard faces on wet-sheened asphalt, cut by the impossible light bleeding out of each wrong window across the sidewalk; the sky pure black above.
